groups.title: Beat 3 · Run it, then measure it

beats.label: Ask it one question
beats.cue: [needs-key] It answers correctly — in prose. The contract wanted `capital=Paris`, and nothing downstream can parse a paragraph.
beats.script: It answers correctly — in prose. The contract wanted `capital=Paris`, and nothing downstream can parse a paragraph. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Single-turn run; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: a correct prose answer ("The capital of France is **Paris**." plus a paragraph), i.e. right city, wrong shape.
beats.command: crewhaus run live/crewhaus.yaml --prompt "What is the capital of France?"

verify.note: single-turn run; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: a correct prose answer ("The capital of France is **Paris**." plus a paragraph), i.e. right city, wrong shape

beats.label: Open the dataset
beats.cue: Ten capital-of-X questions — and every expected_output is the contract line, `capital=<City>`.

beats.label: Open the graders
beats.cue: Two graders, ANDed. `contains` takes a LITERAL substring — the same string for every sample, so it can only check the `capital=` marker. The per-sample check is `exact_match`, which compares against that sample's own expected_output.
beats.script: Two graders, ANDed. `contains` takes a LITERAL substring — the same string for every sample, so it can only check the `capital=` marker. groups.title: One more thing · The patch is the artifact

beats.label: Try the default mutator first
beats.cue: [needs-key] The rule-based provider's whole mutation space is four canned edits — “Be concise and direct.”, one pasted Example:, a swap, a CoT prefix. None of them invents an output contract: “score: 0.000 → 0.000”, and it declines to write.
beats.script: The rule-based provider's whole mutation space is four canned edits — “Be concise and direct.”, one pasted Example:, a swap, a CoT prefix. None of them invents an output contract: “score: 0.000 → 0.000”, and it declines to write. [[pause:1.8s]] Configured provider or platform credentials are required here, so the offline verifier checks the shape but does not execute the call. Re-evals the 3-sample dev split per candidate; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: `[optimize] score: 0.000 → 0.000 (Δ +0.000)` then `no improvement above threshold 0.01; source untouched.`.
beats.command: crewhaus optimize live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset dataset.jsonl --graders graders.yaml --iterations 5 --seed 42 -o live/optimize-rule

verify.note: re-evals the 3-sample dev split per candidate; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0: `[optimize] score: 0.000 → 0.000 (Δ +0.000)` then `no improvement above threshold 0.01; source untouched.` — the deterministic mutator never reaches the `capital=` contract, and the 0.01 gate refuses the no-op patch

beats.label: Let the model-driven mutator try
beats.cue: [needs-key] --mutator claude reads each failing sample's grader rationale and writes the instruction that answers it: “score: 0.000 → 1.000 (Δ +1.000)”, first iteration, about a cent.
beats.script: --mutator claude reads each failing sample's grader rationale and writes the instruction that answers it: “score: 0.000 → 1.000 (Δ +1.000)”, first iteration, about a cent. [[pause:1.8s]] The demo crosses into its live path at this point; with the required credentials loaded, the real runtime performs the work. 3 mutator calls + 4 dev-split evals; needs Anthropic credentials.
beats.command: crewhaus optimize live/crewhaus.yaml --dataset dataset.jsonl --graders graders.yaml --iterations 3 --mutator claude -o live/optimize

verify.note: 3 mutator calls + 4 dev-split evals; needs Anthropic credentials. Measured on CLI 0.4.0, four consecutive runs: `[optimize] score: 0.000 → 1.000 (Δ +1.000)`, `spend: ~$0.011 over 3 model call(s)`, `patch ready (improvement ≥ 0.01)`, `pinned 3 recovered samples → hello-optimize-regressions@v1`
